name: Recovery Code Sign-In Could Not Authenticate
summary: A password-proved returning user submits a TOTP recovery code that is not accepted; no authenticated session is created, the MFA challenge remains available for retry, and the recovery-code entry surface shows a non-enumerating error.

preconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and a password-issued MFA challenge is active for an existing durable identity with confirmed email, enabled TOTP, and recovery codes

inputs.name: Recovery Code
inputs.description: A deliberately invalid or previously consumed recovery code used to prove the rejected outcome.

serverInteraction.intent: Resolve the durable identity held by the password-issued MFA challenge, reject the submitted recovery-code proof without establishing a session, and preserve the outstanding MFA challenge for retry.

postconditions.expression: the durable identity remains active with TOTP enabled, the password-issued MFA challenge remains available for retry, no authenticated session is established, and rejection details are not disclosed

sourceReferences.note: ConsumeRecoveryCodeAsync rejects invalid or unavailable recovery codes without authenticating the user.
The challenge is consumed only after successful recovery proof, so rejection preserves the same outstanding MFA context for retry.
Angular stays on the recovery view and exposes status:recovery-error for rejected proof.
React Native stays on the recovery view and exposes status:recovery-error for rejected proof.
Authored integration proof verifies invalid recovery proof does not consume the MFA challenge or establish a session.
